info.description:
Analyse images with vision-language models.

**Authentication**: every `/v1` endpoint requires `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...`
(click **Authorize** above). Keys are issued with
`python scripts/init_db.py create-key --email you@example.com`.

**Sending images**: `POST /v1/vision` accepts either
* `application/json` with an `image_url` (fetched server-side with SSRF protection), or
* `multipart/form-data` with one or more `images` files (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF).

All images are validated by content, stripped of metadata (EXIF/GPS) and downscaled.

**Sync vs async**: `mode=sync` (default) returns the result directly; `mode=async` returns
`202` with a `job_id` to poll at `GET /v1/jobs/{job_id}`.

**Rate limits**: per user, fixed window. Responses carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`,
`X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`; a `429` includes `Retry-After`.

**Errors** always use one shape:
`{"error": {"type": "...", "message": "...", "param": null}, "request_id": "..."}`.
Quote `request_id` (also in the `X-Request-ID` header) when reporting problems.
info.title: Vision AI API

post.description:
Upload one invoice (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF or a PDF of up to 10 pages) as `multipart/form-data`
field `file`; get back its fields as structured JSON: invoice number and date, seller and
buyer (names, addresses, GSTINs), place of supply, line items and totals.

Every field has a `value` (`null` when it is not on the invoice; nothing is guessed), a
`status` (`ok`, `check` = verify before use, `missing`), a heuristic `confidence`, the
`source_text` it was read from and a `note` explaining any `check`. The OCR model reads the
document; when a reasoning model is configured, it cross-checks the fields. Arithmetic, GST
and amount-in-words checks run on the result (`validation`).

The invoice is stored for review: `id` opens it in the dashboard, and `review_status` says
whether it was approved automatically (confident and every check passed), needs review, or
should be reprocessed.

With `?mode=async` the call returns at once (`202`, `Location: /v1/invoices/{id}`) and the
invoice is read in the background; poll `GET /v1/invoices/{id}`. Use it for multi-page PDFs
and slow (CPU) servers.

Needs the server to run PaddleOCR-VL (see README, "GGUF models with llama.cpp"). Processing
takes seconds per page on a GPU and a few minutes per page on a CPU. Billed like one
`/v1/vision` request, by the tokens both models used.

get.description:
Poll an async job created by `POST /v1/vision` with `mode=async`.

Status lifecycle: `pending` -> `processing` -> `completed` | `failed`.
- `completed`: `result` holds the same payload as a synchronous response.
- `failed`: `error` holds a client-safe reason; `result` is `null`.

Jobs are private to the user who created them. Anyone else gets `404`, exactly as for a
job that does not exist, so job ids cannot be probed. Polling is not rate limited; an
interval of 1-2 seconds is reasonable.

post.description:
Analyse one or more images with a vision-language model.

**Authentication**: `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...` (use **Authorize** above).
**Rate limit**: per user; see the `X-RateLimit-*` response headers. A `429` includes `Retry-After`.

### Two ways to send images

**1. `multipart/form-data`** to upload files. Repeat the `images` field for several files,
optionally together with an `image_url`:

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/vision \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -F prompt="Describe this image" -F images=@photo.jpg
```

**2. `application/json`** to analyse an image by URL (fetched server-side):

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/vision \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt": "Describe this image", "image_url": "https://httpbin.org/image/png"}'
```

### Limits
- 1 to 4 images per request (uploads + URL); JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF (first frame only).
- Each image at most 10 MB and 40 megapixels. Type is detected from content, never from the file name.
- Images are stripped of all metadata (EXIF/GPS) and downscaled before inference.

### Sync vs async
- `mode=sync` (default): **200** with the result.
- `mode=async`: **202** with a `job_id` (and a `Location` header); poll `GET /v1/jobs/{job_id}`.
  Requests that are invalid up front (no image, unknown model, bad parameters) are rejected
  immediately without creating a job.
